FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard ( Third Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Cranes Lifting Chains and its Related Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical 
Engineering Division Council. 

This standard was originally published in 1965 and subsequently revised in 1977 and 1999. In this revision all the 
amendments have been incorporated and the following major changes have been made: 


a) To help standardization, as far as possible, relating requirements for components to basic duty factor for 
class of mechanisms. 

b) Recommended selection of group mechanism (duty class) of the crane for purchaser. 

c) Simplified graphical method for calculating permissible fatigue stress. 

d) Selection of wheel and giving due consideration of duty class, travel speed and wheel material. 

e) Selection of sizes for wire rope, rope drum, sheave and allowable fleet angle using graphical method. 


f) Provision of compacted rope, seamless pipe for rope drum, case carburized gearboxes, geared brake 
motor, etc. have been made. 


g) Motor selection with thermal adequacy, use of service factor and RMS method has been prescribed. 


h) The mechanism duty is classified in eight groups M1 to M8 based on their total duration of utilization 
applying upto the time of replacement of mechanism and load spectrum that is, life load cycle. 


j) Certain other changes for better implementation of the standard. 


The requirements of IS 4137 : 2015 ‘Heavy duty electric overhead travelling cranes including special service 
machines for use in steel work — Code of practice’ has been covered in this revision. This Indian Standard 
supersedes the IS 4137: 2015. 


This standard covers design, manufacture and erection of electric overhead traveling cranes and gantry cranes 
for use in steel works and other locations. The standard also covers mechanical, electrical, inspection and testing 
aspects as related to design, manufacture and erection of electric overhead traveling cranes in order to secure 
safe, efficient and reliable working of these heavy duty cranes during service. Structural design aspects of all 
types of cranes and hoists are covered in IS 807 : 2006 ‘Design, erection and testing (structural portion) of cranes 
and hoists — Code of practice. Cranes are broadly classified into eight classes in IS 807 depending on duty and 
number of hours in service per year. 


The new classification of cranes now coming into effect and the classification presently in use can approximately 
be compared as follows: 


Old Equivalent | New Classification Average Working Average Total Life in 
Hours Per Day Working Hours, Min 
I МІ 0.5-4 400 
M2 800 
M3 1 600 
II M4 4-6 3 200 
М5 6 300 
Ш М6 6-9 25 000 
IV M7 6-9 35 000 
M8 12 75 000 


NOTE — The running time per day and total life relate to mechanism class only. 


(Continued on third cover)

SECTION 1 GENERAL 
1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard covers requirements for design, 
manufacture, inspection and testing of electric 
overhead travelling cranes and gantry cranes for use in 
steel works and other locations. Its provisions where 
applicable, shall also apply to special purpose cranes, 
such as, those listed in Annex A including steel plant 
crane and other overhead travelling cranes, portal 
and semi-portal cranes, single girder, double girder or 
mono-box type (Fig. 1). It is recommended that, the 
crane should be designed based on the duty classes and 
application, irrespective of usage in steel works or at 
other locations. Classification of the crane as a whole 
shall be taken as defined from classes Al, A2, ...... A8 
and as defined as from mechanism classes M1, M2, ..... 
М8 classification as defined in foreword. Structural 
design aspects of all types of cranes and hoists are 
covered in IS 807. 


1.2 The duty class of crane preferably be selected as 
per 1.1. 


1.3 Annex B gives guidance which may be referred by 
purchaser while specifying the duty class. 


1.4 This standard is not intended for application to 
cranes for use in areas where sparks from cranes could 
lead to explosions. 


1.5 It is recommended that IS 13367 (Part 1) to be 
referred for safe usage of crane. 


1.6 Risk assessment and risk reduction to be carried out 
as per IS 16819 and IS 16504 (Part 1) if agreed between 
the manufacturer and the purchaser. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex C contain provisions, 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 


possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards indicated in Annex C. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


3.1 General — For the purpose of this standard the 
definitions given in IS 13473 (Part 1) and following text 
shall apply. If there are common terms, the definitions 
given in this standard shall prevail. 


3.2 Normal Service Condition — Normal service 
condition shall satisfy the following conditions: 


a) Indoor and outdoor applications should with 
normal air of normal humidity and free from 
contamination; 


b) Ambient temperature should be 0°C to 40°C and if 
the service conditions those beyond this, suitable 
derating factors shall be applied; and 


с) Altitude should not exceed 1 000 m above mean 
sea level. 


4 TECHNICAL INFORMATION ТО ВЕ 
PROVIDED 


4.1 Information to be Supplied with Enquiry or 
Order 


Information regarding the conditions under which 
the crane is to be used, together with the information 
required in Annex D, shall be supplied with the enquiry 
or order. 


4.2 Information to be Supplied by the Manufacturer 
with Offer 


The manufacturer shall supply all technical details/ 
documents together with the information required in 
Annex E including drawings giving the over all sizes, 
clearance, end approaches, structural features, travel 
wheel loads, type of buffers, impact forces, wheel 
spacing, etc. 


5 IDENTIFICATION 


5.1 A small plate shall be located in a prominent 
position in the cabin or suitable location bearing the

5.1.1 In general purpose cranes, X/Y indicates the 
following: 

a) X — Capacity of the main hook, in tonnes; and 

b) Y — Capacity of the auxiliary hook, in tonnes. 
Both the hoists are mounted on one trolley (double 
girder). 
5.1.2 X + Y indicates the following: 

a) X — Capacity of the main hoist in tonnes; and 

b) Y — Capacity of the main auxiliary hoist, in 

tonnes. 


Main hoist is mounted on main trolley and the auxiliary 
hoist on a separate auxiliary trolley and both the trolleys 
may be on same girder (double girder) or on different 
girders (four girders). 


5.1.3 X/Y/Z indicates the following: 
a) X — Capacity of the main hoist, in tonnes; 
b) Y — Capacity of the auxiliary hook 1; and 
c) Z— Capacity of the auxiliary hook 2. 
All hooks are mounted on one trolley (double girder). 


5.1.4 X + Y / Z indicates the following: 
a) X — Capacity of the main hoist, in tonnes; 


b) Y — Capacity of the main hook of the auxiliary 
trolley; and 


c) Z—Capacity of the auxiliary hook of the auxiliary 
trolley. 


Main hoist hooks are mounted on one trolley and both 
the hooks of auxiliary trolley are mounted on another 
trolley and both the trolleys may be on same girder 
(double girder) or on different girders (four girders for 
ladle cranes). 


5.2 Rating Plate 


a) The lifting capacity shall be permanently marked 
in a visible position and shall be easily legible 
from the ground; 


b) In case of grabbing cranes, the lifting capacity 
shall be permissible total weight of the grab and 
the lifting capacity; and 

c) Inthe case of cranes with more than one hoist, the 
lifting capacity of each hoist shall be indicated on 
the relevant hook block. 


5.3 Manufacturer’s Name Plate 


The manufacturer’s name plate shall contain the 
following details: 


a) Name of manufacture; 
b) Year of manufacture; 
c) Manufacturer serial number; and 
d) Safe working load of each hoist shall be 
permanently marked on each side of crane in such 
a manner as to be easily legible from the floor and 
in tonnes; 
5.4 Warning Notices 
The following warning notices shall be suitably located 
so as to be clearly visible: 
a) Do not stand under the load; 
b) No access for unauthorized personnel; and 


c) Danger-crane; by means of warning colour strips 
(as applicable). 


6 WORKMANSHIP, 
INSPECTION 


MATERIAL AND 


6.1 Workmanship and material shall be subject to the 
inspection of the owner or his representative at all 
times. Weldments of carbon steel (except bridge girder, 
trolley structure, boggie, end carriage) shall be stress 
relieved by uniformly heating in a furnace, wherever 
applicable. Field welds shall likewise be stress relieved 
unless other means agreeable to the owner as specified 
in the information sheet. The temperature of the 
furnace when the weldment is placed in it shall not be 
over 150°C at the start and increased to 650°C at a rate 
not exceeding 95°C/h, and then held at the temperature 
for 1 h/25 mm of thickness of material. It shall then be 
cooled in the furnace at a rate (not exceeding 95°C/h) 
to 260°C, before being removed from the furnace. 
Weldments of alloy material shall be welded and stress 
relieved using a procedure as per IS 16003 or ASME, 
Sec - ІХ. 


6.2 The stress relieving shall be applicable for the 
plate thickness of more than 40 mm as per AWS 14.1 
or ASME Section VIII, Div I. For larger components 
where the thermal stress relieving is not possible, as 
an alternative, the mechanical vibratory method shall 
be applied. To stress relieve the field weld, local flame 
heating shall be applied. 


6.3 Safety Clearances 


All moving parts of the cranes shall be at least 100 mm 
from any fixed part of a building/structure and minimum 
of 600 mm from human access area. Alternatively, the 
safety clearances shall be as per agreement between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer. 


SECTION 2 MECHANICAL 
COMPONENTS 


7 DESIGN PROCEDURE 


7.1 General 


The design of the component parts of the mechanism 
relating to each crane motion shall be included with 
due allowance for the effects of the duty which the 
mechanism shall perform in service. The design of 
the component parts will be in accordance with the 
provisions given in this section. 


7.2 Load Amplifying Factor 


The load amplifying factor applied to the motion of 
the hook in a vertical direction covers inertia forces 
including shock. In calculating fatigue analysis in the 
components of the mechanism the live loads, the rated 
hook load shall be multiplied by the load amplifying 
factor, given in Table 1. 

NOTE — Load amplifying factor for structural design shall be 

as per IS 807. Table 1 refers for fatigue design of mechanical 

components only.

(for Fatigue Analysis)

7.3 Loadings to be Considered іп the Design of 
Mechanisms 


7.3.1 Loads 


The following loadings shall be taken into account 
when designing a mechanism and its components: 


R = Loads due to the dead weight of the mechanism 
or component and dead weight of those parts 
of the crane acting on the mechanism or the 
component under consideration. 


= Loads due to the weight of the hook load with 
reference to Fig. 2 and also it is defined as 
SWL of the hook. 


= Loads due to the weight of the hook load 
increased by the load amplifying factor given 
in 7.2. 


Dynamic loading arising from the acceleration 
or braking of the motion and from skewing 
interaction between the crane and track. These 
loads include those loads due to the following 
reasons: 
a) inertia of the mechanism, associated crane 
parts and hook load; 
b) its prime mover and brakes; and 
c) concurrent operation of other motions, etc, 
as applicable. 
Loads arising from frictional forces. 
Loads due to the service wind acting 
horizontally in any direction where applicable 
according to IS 807. 
Loads arising out of wind pressure during 
out of service condition with wind acting 


horizontally in any direction where applicable 
according to IS 875 (Part 3). 


Loads due to collision with end buffers.

BUCKET 


LIFTING ATTACHMENT

7.3.2 Loading Condition апа Load Combinations 


Each mechanism of the crane shall be designed to 
operate satisfactorily under the most unfavourable 
combination of loadings that can occur under different 
conditions and that could also actually occur in practice. 


7.3.2.1 Case I - Normal service without wind where 
crane capacity equal to R 
а) Vertical Motion — Hoisting or lowering: 
1) R +R +R +R;or 
2) Rit Ry 
b) Horizontal Motion — Traverse or travel: 
R tR, +R +R, 
7.3.2.2 Case II - Normal service with wind 
a) Vertical Motion — Hoisting or lowering: 
D R+R +R. +R AR; or 
2) A Ret Ra 


hi 


b) Horizontal Motion — Traverse or travel: 
RTRTR TR+R. 


7.3.2.3 Case III Crane out of service 


a) Vertical Motion — Hoisting or lowering not 
applicable. 


b) Horizontal Motion — Traverse or travel : 
R, + Ry 
7.3.2.4 Case IV — Exceptional loading condition 


The combination of loads to be considered for this 
case of loading will depend upon the type of crane, 
application and the crane motion. Account shall be 
taken of any loading condition that are known to apply 
but which are not covered under the other three cases 
of loading. A few cases of exceptional loading are as 
follows: 


a) Loads due to collision of cranes with each other or 
with end stoppers that is buffer loads; 


b) Loads due to testing of cranes; 
c) Erection loads; and 


d) Loads due to the maximum load that the motor can 
actually transmit to the mechanism while starting, 
stalling or due to higher actual power. 


7.4 Design Procedure 


7.4.1 General 


Mechanism components shall be proportioned by 
checking that they have adequate safety against 
becoming unserviceable as a result of a single 
combination of extreme loading conditions causing 
fracture, bending or other type of failures. They 
shall also be checked whenever appropriate against 
fatigue, deflection or over heating. In this connection, 


consideration shall be given to the consequences of 
failure. For example, failure in hoisting mechanism 
component is usually more dangerous occurrences than 
failure of a horizontal motion mechanism. 


7.4.2 Basis of Design 


Mechanism components are checked depending on the 
ultimate strength by verifying that the calculated stress 
does not exceed a permissible stress dependent on the 
breaking strength of the material used. 

NOTE — If, C, is considered in calculation of allowable 


strength then load amplifying factor as mentioned in 7.2 need 
not to be considered. 


7.4.3 Permissible Stress 


Mechanism component shall be checked for strength 
under case I, II, III and IV loading conditions and 
load combinations specified in 7.3.2. The value of the 
permissible stress F, is given by following formula 
where unit of stress was defined as N/mm*: 


Ж = P 


Car ^ C, XC. 


Where, 
F „= ultimate tensile strength of the material; 
С,- duty factor for the appropriate mechanism 
class. For the values see Table 2; 
C,,= basic stress factor corresponding to each case 
of loading. For the values see Table 3; and 
C „= safety factor depending on the material used. 


For the values see Table 4. 


7.4.3.1 Permissible stress Fa should be reduced by 
20 percent in the crane component for reverse bending. 


7.4.3.2 Normally, the steel plant cranes are designed for 
M6, М7 and М8 class duty which need to be checked 
against fatigue / endurance limit. The working stress is 
to be calculated based on below formula, 


Working stress — Stress due to rated load x stress 
concentration factor х load amplifying factor. 


That is, for bending: 
horn Syr X K x Load amplifying factor (as per Table 1) 
Where,

7.4.5 Checking for Fatigue 
7.4.5.1 General 


Where it is necessary to check a component for fatigue, 
recognized techniques available for calculation of 
fatigue properties shall be used. The choice of the 
methods used shall be left to the manufacturer, however, 
he shall specify the origin of the methods to be adopted, 
if asked by the customer.

7.4.5.2 Loading condition 


Case I of loading condition as specified in 7.3.2 shall be 
used as the basis for all fatigue checks. 


7.4.5.3 Factors affecting fatigue strength 


For any component, the magnitude of the permissible 
fatigue stress ( p) depends upon the following factors: 


a) Total number of stress cycles during the service 
life of the component ‘n’; 


b) Type of stress cycles (that is, degree of stress 
fluctuation); 


c) Quality of the material; 
d) Size of the component; 
e) Surface finish of the component; 


f) Configuration of the individual details under 
consideration; and 


g) Miscellaneous effects such as the effects of 
corrosion, residual stress, electrolytic plating, 
metal spraying, etc, where under certain conditions 
reduce the permissible fatigue stress. 7.4.5.4 gives 
a method for calculating the fatigue reference 
stress (р,) which takes account from the factor (а) 


to (g). 


NOTE — A check for fatigue need not be made in the cases, 
where experience shows that the ultimate strength check as per 
7.4.3 is sufficient. 


7.4.5.4 Stresses 


The following characteristics shall be determined for 
each type of fluctuating stress, for example, tension, 
compression, bending or shear, occurring during an 
appropriate stress cycle in the component detail having 
regard to the loading that it will experience: 


po з: Е

in the stress cycle;

opposite sense to fy, 
рь Permissible fatigue stress, іп

P= Fatigue reference stress at which a 


component detail has a 90 percent 
probability of survival;

7.4.5.5 Permissible fatigue stress 


When single nature of stresses are applicable, then the 
working stress should be less than permissible fatigue 
stress which is to be calculated as per 7.4.3.2 . 


The stress combination occurring most frequently in 
practice in a component detail is that of bending and 
torsion. The details subjected to this combination shall 
be designed so that: 


Cf, valt, y + (f, T РЫ «1.0 


7.4.5.6 Checking for crippling 


Component subjected to crippling that is overall 
flexural buckling due to axial compression shall be 
checked so that the calculated stress does not exceed 
a limit stress determined as a function of critical stress 
above which there is a risk of crippling occurring. For 
this check coefficient С, as given in Table 2 shall be 
taken into account. 


7.4.5.7 Checking for wear 


In the case of parts subjected to wear, the specific 
physical quantities, such as, surface pressure or 
the circumferential velocity must be determined. 
The figures must be such that on the basis of OEM/ 
international practices they will not lead to excessive 
wear. 


7.4.5.8 Means of access 


7.4.5.8.1 General requirements 


In front of the panel the working place shall be 
minimum of 500 mm or width of the door of the panel 
or whichever is more. Safe means of access shall be 
provided to the driver’s cabin and to every place where 
any person engaged on the inspection, repair and 


15 3177 :2020 


lubrication of the crane will be called upon to work, 
adequate handholds and footholds being provided 
where necessary. 


7.4.5.8.2 Platforms 


Every platform shall be securely fenced with double 
tiered guard rails having a minimum height of 1.1 m 
and toe boards, unless parts of the crane structure 
provided safely. The platform normal width with only 
chequered plates shall be of sufficient to enable normal 
maintenance work to be carried out safely. On bridge 
platform, minimum clear width which shall be not less 
than 0.50 m in normal width, the fencing shall extend 
along the full length of the outer edge. Guard rails on 
the trolley side of the bridge platform may be provided, 
if required. 


7.4.5.8.3 Ladders 


Sides of ladders shall extend about | m above top rung, 
unless some other appropriate handhold is provided. 
Ladders shall if possible, slope forward. Vertical ladders 
exceeding 3 m in length shall be provided with back 
safety guards. The ladders over 5 m in height should 
be provided with safety hoops starting at a height of 
2.5 m. The distance between safety hoops shall not be 
greater than 0.9 m. The strength of safety hoops must 
be adequate to withstand a force of 100 kg distributed 
over 100 mm acting on any point of the loop. The 
ladders must be provided with rest platforms spaced so 
that the first stretch does not exceed 10 m and there are 
then rest platforms at every 8 m. 


7.4.5.8.4 Stair ways 


Slope of stairways should preferably be 45°, however 
shall not exceed 60° (with horizontal), the height of 
individual steps shall not exceed 250 mm and their 
depth shall not be less than 150 mm the surface of treads 
shall be anti-slip. The stair ways shall be provided with 
guard rails on each side. 


NOTE — In case of space constraint, slope of stairways may 
be mutually decided by the purchaser and the manufacturer. 


8 HOOKS 


8.1 The hook material and rated capacity shall be selected 
from IS 15560, IS 5749, and DIN 15407-1 or AISE 7 
(for Laminated hooks). DIN 15400 for single point 
and Ramshorn hooks are also acceptable. Radiography 
test may be done for forged hook, if mutually agreed 
between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 


8.2 General 


Hooks shall be designed for the rated load. The design 
shall be established by analysis or testing as per relevant 
standards. 


8.3 Details 


Hooks shall be forged from fine grained material. 
Any welding on the hook shall be with the approval 


12 


of qualified welding engineer and performed prior 
to initial heat treatment. The capacity of hook may 
be stamped on the hook nose. The hook shall not be 
painted. 


8.4 Hook Body 


Hook bodies shall be of standard design where the 
line of resultant load on the hook passes through the 
centre of curvature of the inside edge of the hook and 
coincides with the centerline of the shank. 


8.5 Testing 


A certificate of compliance showing static load testing 
(proof load test ) covering the configuration of the hook 
body and the hook shank shall be provided. 


8.6 Latches 


Hook latches and swivel lock plates shall be provided 
when specified. 


8.7 Mounting 


Swiveling hooks shall be mounted on thrust bearings. 
A protective skirt shall be provided to enclose the 
bearings. The thrust bearings shall be provided with 
facilities for lubrication. 


9 WIRE ROPES 


9.1 The hoisting ropes shall be of the grade and type 
specified in IS 2266. Steel cored ropes shall be used 
for cranes handling hot metal or where the rope has 
to be used under water or in corrosive atmosphere. 
All wire ropes shall generally be of ordinary lay, right 
hand, pre-formed and ungalvanized. For grab cranes 
one rope may have left hand lay and the other right 
hand lay or non-rotating rope according to IS 2266. 
The compacted ropes suitable for crane duty may be 
used as per agreement between the purchaser and the 
supplier based on various crane’s application. Ropes 
working under water and in corrosive atmosphere shall 
be galvanized. Reverse bend in the rope reeving shall 
be avoided as far as possible. The sheave arrangement 
should be reeved so as to eliminate reverse bends 
preferably except at the drum and equilizer. 


9.2 The maximum allowable fleet angle for frequent 
working positions shall be 3° for all classes of cranes. 
However, maximum allowable fleet angle for seldom 
reach position may be permitted upto 5°. Fig 6 may be 
referred for further guidance with respect to rope speed. 


The negative fleet angle can be calculated based on 
below formula: Negative fleet angle = Allowable 
positive fleet angle —tan `! ( Pitch of the groove / 3.14 x 
rope PCD on the drum ) 


When special reeving, such as, a stabilized reeving 
arrangement is used, consideration must be given to 
geometry and dynamics to maintain the appropriate 
safety factors. Provisions should be made to prevent 
the twisting of the hook block.

designing hoist drums the following should be taken 
into consideration.

9.6 Strength of Rope Drum 


Drums shall be designed to withstand the compressive 
stress caused by the wound of wire rope, bending stress 
due to beam action and torsional stress. 


All rope drum shall be checked against crushing stress 
and permissible compressive stress at the groove when 
rope is wound on drum. 


The rope drum which manufactured from E-250 grade 
of IS 2062 or ASTM A 106 Gr. A or B material or any 
other equivalent standard, the minimum permissible 
crushing stress will be 1100 kg/cm? for M7 and 
М8 duty cranes and 1250 kg/cm’ for МІ to M6 duty 
cranes. 


If rope drum manufactured from E-350 grade of 
IS 2062 than the minimum permissible crushing 
stress will be 1 350 kg/cm? for M7 and М8 duty cranes 
and 1 500 kg/cm? for МІ to M6 duty cranes. 


Normally, the rope drum is safe in bending and torsion 
but longer rope drum should be checked against 
bending and torsion. 


The seamless pipe has more strength against fabricated 
drum manufactured from steel plates. The grain 
structures are in circumferential direction in seamless 
pipe, which is better for withstanding compressive 
stress. As compressive stress is the prime criteria in 
rope drum design. 


9.7 General 


Drums shall be designed for single layer of ropes 
only and can be designed with multilayer guided rope 
when agreed to between the manufacturer and the 
purchaser. 


9.8 Length of the Drum 


The drum shall be of such length that each lead of 
wire rope has a minimum of two full turns on the 
drum when hook is at its lowest position not taking 
into consideration the turns covered by the wire rope 
anchorage and one spare groove for each lead of the 
wire rope on the drum when hook is at its highest 
position. 


In the case where the drum flanges are not provided, 
a free length not less than 4 times to the diameter of 
the wire rope or 100 mm dia whichever is more is to 
be provided beyond the last groove center line at the 
anchorage point. 


9.9 Flanges 


The drums shall be flanged at one or both ends in the 
following conditions such as: 
a) For single flange drum, at the end where wire rope 
is released. 
b) For drums having handed grooves at both ends if 
wire ropes are released from the end of drums. 
c) For multi-layer wire ropes at both ends. 
d) If required by the purchaser. 


Where provided, the flanges shall project above the 
wire rope to a distance not less than 2 times of the wire 
rope diameter or 50 mm whichever is less beyond the 
wound rope. 


IS 3177 : 2020 


9.10 Grooving of the Drum 


Rope drums shall have machined grooves and the 
contour at the bottom of the grooves shall be circular 
over a minimum angle of 130?. The lead of the rope 
shall not exceed 5? ( 1 in 12 ) on either side of the helix 
angle of the groove in the drum. 


Grooving shall be finished smooth and shall be free 
from surface defects likely to injure the wire rope. The 
edges between the grooves shall be rounded. The radius 
of the groove shall be between 0.5254 to 0.550 d (with 
0.537d as the optimum see Fig. 7) times the diameter 
of the wire rope rounded off upwards to the nearest 
0.5 mm. The depth of the groove shall not be less than 
0.35 (for crane duty upto M 5) or 0.4 (for crane duty 
above M 5) times the diameter of the wire ropes for 
drum with single layer of the wire rope. 
The grooves of the drum shall be so pitched that there 
is a clearance between adjacent turns of the rope of not 
less than: 
а) 1.5 mm for ropes up to and including 12 mm 
diameter, 
b) 2.5 mm for ropes above 12 mm diameter and 
including 28 mm diameter, and 
с) 3.0 mm for ropes above 28 mm diameter. 
The depth of the groove shall not be less than 0.2 times 


the diameter of the wire rope for multiple layers of wire 
rope on the drum. The pitch of the grooves of the drum

Nominal diameter of rope

shall not be less than 1.05 times the diameter of the 
wire rope for multiple layers of the wire rope on the 
drum. 


9.11 Material for the Drum 


Drums shall be made of seamless pipe as per ASTM A 
106 GR A or B, cast iron of minimum Grade 25, cast 
steel, rolled steel of welded construction and in case of 
welded drum this should be stress relieved. 


9.12 Rope Anchorage 


The end of the wire rope shall be anchored to the drum 
in such a way that the anchorage is readily accessible. 
Each wire rope shall have not less than two full turns on 
the drums when the hook is at the lowest position not 
taking into consideration the turns covered by the wire 
rope anchorage. 


10 SHEAVES 


10.1 The minimum pitch diameter of sheaves for all 
crane class shall be selected based on formula given in 
9.5. Use the next larger size diameter for lead sheave. 
Sheaves shall be enclosed by guards which fit close 
to the flanges to prevent the ropes from coming out 
of the grooves. The material of the sheaves shall be 
as per IS 1030. The bearing assembly in each sheaves 
shall be individually lubricated. The fittings and grease 
lines shall be located so that they will be protected 
from damage. Where possible, upper sheave block 
mountings shall be above the trolley deck. The upper 
sheaves block shall be removable as a unit from the 
above. The diameter at the bottom of the groove may 
be selected from the preferred values that is, 125, 160, 
200, 250, 320, 400, 500, 560, 630, 710, 800, 900, 1 000 
and 1 120 mm. 


10.2 Grooving 


Sheaves shall have machined groove. The contour 
at the bottom of the groove shall be circular over a 
minimum angle of 130° and shall have an included 
angle of 45° to 60? proportional to fleet angle of rope. 
The depth of the groove shall not be less than 1.5 times 
the diameter of the rope. The radius of the groove shall 
be between 0.525 to 0.550 times the diameter of the 
wire rope rounded of upwards to the nearest 0.5 mm 
on higher side. 


11 EQUALIZER BARS OR SHEAVES 


Where required, either an equalizer bar or sheave 
will be acceptable. In either case the bar or sheaves 
shall be positioned to be accessible from the floor of 
the trolley and made in such manner that it can turn 
or swivel to align itself with the pull of the ropes. The 
minimum pitch diameter of equalizer sheaves shall be 
selected based on formula given in 9.5. Cranes having 
hoists which handle hot metal or critical loads should 


16 


utilize equalizer bars to provide two independent rope 
systems, not equalizer sheaves. For increased rope life, 
consideration shall be given to using equalizer sheaves 
with the same diameter as the running sheave. The 
diameter shall be selected from the below preferred 
values, 125, 160, 200, 250, 320, 400, 500, 560 and 
630 mm. 


12 TRACK WHEELS 


12.1 General 


All track wheels shall be double flanged. Incase of 
under slung crane bridge wheel and in single girder 
cross travel wheel may be of single flange.The wheel 
shall be made by roll forming, forging or casting from 
grades of steel appropriate to the forming process. 
The wheel can also be made from forged tyre shrunk 
on cast steel, if agreed between the purchaser and the 
manufacturer. Bridge track wheels shall have either 
straight or tapered treads. The material of the wheels 
shall be of grade C55Mn75 of IS 1570 (Part 1 and 
Part 2/Sec 2) or 42CrMo4 or equivalent. Bridge 
wheel loads (P... and P in) shall be determined with 
the maximum lifted load on the trolley, which shall 
be positioned at the closest working approach that 
produces the maximum wheel load. Trolley wheel 
loads shall be determined with the maximum lifted 
loads: 


Maximum lift load = (W, + W + W) 


Where, 
= Total weight of trolley including mast if any, 
W = weight of the lifted load, and 


L 


W,= Weight of lifting appliances if any. 
12.2 Wheel Hardness 


The hardness of the wheel rim shall be maintained 
between 300 and 350 BHN with minimum depth of 10 
mm. If hardness ofthe wheel rim more than 350 BHN is 
required, it shall be decided as per agreement between 
the purchaser and the crane supplier. The limiting 
pressure value (Р) of wheel materials are mentioned 
in Table 6 which is to be considered while selection of 
wheel diameter. 


In case, if crane wheels are to be manufactured from 
alloy steel or high tensile steel and treated to ensure 
very high surface hardness, the value of P, is limited 
to that for the quality of the steel comprising the 
wheel prior to surface treatment according to Table 6. 
The higher value of wheel hardness will give better 
life however, would risk causing wear of the rail and 
possibility of crack generation during shock loads. The 
hardening of the wheel tread at the depth of 0.01 D 
may be taken into account when selecting the value 
of P.

Dimensions of flanges for guiding tread wheels at the

12.7 Width of Tread 


The width of the wheel tread shall be greater than the 
rail head by an amount which shall suitably allow for 
the variations in the gantry rail alignment, gantry track 
span dimensions and crane span dimensions. 


12.8 Adhesion of the Drive Wheels 


To eliminate slipping of the drive wheels of the travelling 
mechanism of the crane or crab, the design shall be 
checked for adhesion under the most unfavourable 
combination of loads producing maximum апа 
minimum loads on the drive wheels. The co-efficient 
of adhesion (friction) shall be taken as 0.2 for dry rails 
and 0.15 for damp rails. 


13 BUFFERS 


13.1 Provisions in the design of the runway and the 
design of the runway stops shall consider the energy 
absorbing or storage device used in the crane bumper. 
The device may be non-linear (for example, hydraulic 
bumpers) or a linear device, such as, a coil spring. 
Other types of buffers like hydraulic and resilient 
plastic buffers may also be used subject to agreement 
between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 


13.2 Buffers shall have sufficient energy absorbing 
capacity to bring unloaded crane / trolley ( loaded crane 
in the case of stiff masted cranes ) to rest from a speed 
of 50 percent of the rated speed at a deceleration rate 
not exceeding 5 m/s?. 


13.3 Between cranes or trolleys (if two trolleys are 
located on one bridge) bumpers shall be capable of 
absorbing the energy from 70 percent of full load rated 
speed of both cranes or trolleys travelling in opposite 
directions, or the energy from 100 percent of full load 
rated speed of either crane or trolley, whichever is the 
greatest. 


18 


13.4 The design of all bumpers shall include safety 
cables to prevent parts from dropping to the floor. For 
computing bridge bumper energy, the trolley shall be 
placed in the end approach which will produce the 
maximum end reaction from both bridge and trolley. 
This end reaction shall be used as the maximum weight 
portion of the crane that can act on each bridge bumper. 
The energy absorbing capacity of the bumper shall be 
based on power-off and shall not include the lifted load, 
If free to swing. Bridge bumpers shall have a contact 
surface of not less than 125 mm in diameter, be located 
on the rail centreline and mounted to provide proper 
clearance when bumpers of two cranes come together 
and both are fully compressed. Where practical, they 
shall be mounted to provide for easy removal of bridge 
track wheels. 


13.5 If required by the customer, buffer may be 
designed at 0.7 times of the rated speed. 


14 SHAFTS 


14.1 General 


Hoist shafting design torque shall be based on the torque 
required to lift the rated load plus hook block and/ 
or lifting beam and shall take account of mechanical 
efficiencies. Design torque for all travel drives shall 
be based on 2 times the 60 min motor rating for series 
wound, constant potential d.c. drives, and 1.7 times 
the 60 min motor rating for a.c. motors and adjustable 
voltage d.c. drives without motor field weakening, 
or wheel slip at maximum wheel load (0.20 friction 
factor), whichever is lower. Due consideration shall 
be given to the maximum brake torque which can be 
applied to the drive. Axles or shafts which are provided 
with sleeve bearings are to be surface or case-hardened 
and ground. 


14.2 Shaft Material 


АП shafts shall be made of low alloy steel in addition to 
C 45 and axles shall have strength, rigidity and required 
the bearing surfaces. All rigid shafts shall be supported 
on two bearings. Angular deflection of the line shaft 
at torque corresponding to 1.5 times the motor torque 
during the acceleration period shall not be more than 
0.3? / m of shaft length. The drive for line shaft shall 
be mounted as close as practicable to the centre of the 
span. 


14.3 Stress Calculations 


АП shafting shall be designed to meet the stresses 
uncounted in actual operation. Due consideration shall 
be given to the maximum torque which may be applied 
to the shaft. When significant stresses are produced 
by the other forces, these forces shall be positioned 
to provide the maximum stresses at the section under 
consideration. Impact shall not be included wherein С, 
value has been considered. 


14.4 Fatigue Stress Check for Normal Operating 
Conditions 


Any shafting subjected to fluctuating stresses, such as, 
the bending or rotating shafts or the torsion in reversing 
drives must be checked for fatigue. The bearing stress 
must not exceed 50 percent of the minimum yield 
strength for non-rotating shafting. 


15 PRESS FITS AND KEYS 


All gears, pinions and couplings shall be pressed and 
keyed and/or shrunk onto shafts. АП press fits shall 
be made in accordance with IS 2048. All keys and 
keyways shall be radiused and/or chamfered according 
to relevant Indian Standard. 


16 BEARINGS 


16.1 Anti-friction bearing shall be used throughout 
except where specified otherwise or mutually agreed. 
Anti-friction bearing shall be self aligning spherical 
roller for wheel and self aligning spherical roller/ taper 
roller/ ball bearing for all gear boxes and cylindrical 
roller/ ball bearing for pulley as per duty class. Anti- 
friction bearing shall be selected for minimum 10 years 
life. The minimum bearing life (in hours) as per their 
class duty are mentioned below: 


Duty Class Minimum Bearing Life 
(in hours) 
MI 1250 
M2 1 250 
M3 2 500 
M4 6 300 
М5 10 000 
М6 15 000 
М7 30 000 
М8 50 000 


Antifriction bearing to be checked for the static load to 
which it can be subjected under whichever of loading 
cases L II or III (see 7.3.2 ) is the most unfavourable. 
Bearing selection in this specification is based on the 
total number of cycles which it is expected the bearing 
will undergo during the number of hours service the 
crane will be used in a 10 year period. 


16.2 All bearings selected shall meet the required 
life at bearing load (at rated speed) based on bearing 
manufacturer. If the load on the bearing is essentially 
constant, the bearings must meet a required life of 
100 percent of the maximum load at rated speed. In 
some cases axle sizes establish bearing sizes. With 
wheel bearings of the antifriction type, one bearing on 
each wheel axle shall be of the fixed type. The other 


19 


IS 3177 : 2020 


bearing shall be arranged to allow for expansion or float 
of the axle. 


16.3 Lubrications 


Provisions shall be made for the service lubrication of 
all the bearings unless sealed and lubricated for life. 
Ball and roller bearings shall be lubricated before 
assembly. Gear housings shall be split or designed to 
permit easy removal of the shaft. Gear reduction units 
should be designed so that gears, shafts and bearings, 
can be pre-assembled as a spare. 


16.4 Bearing Brackets and Housing 


Bearing brackets, if not integral with the frame, shall 
be mounted on a machined surface and be kept in 
alignment by fitted bolts or other equally effective 
methods. When shafting is geared together the support 
structure for all bearing cartridges should, where 
practical, be integral and located as close as possible 
to the gears and pinions. Heavy caps shall be provided 
with a means for lifting. 


17 GEARING 


17.1 Gearing Types 


Gearing shall be spur, herring bone, helical as specified 
in the IS 4460 (Part 1 to 3), IS 7504. No split gears 
shall be used. As far as possible overhung gears should 
be avoided. 


17.2 Gearing Design 


Horsepower ratings for all spur and helical involute 
gearing shall be based upon American Gear 
Manufacturers Association or IS 4460 (Part 1 to 3). 


17.3 Gear Design Loading 


Hoist gear loading for bending strength and pitting 
resistance shall be based on the torque required to lift the 
rated load plus hook block and/or lifting beam. Travel 
drive gear ratings for bending strength and pitting 
resistance shall be based on 2 times the 60 min motor 
rating for series wound constant potential d.c. drives, 
and 1.7 times the 60 min motor rating for a.c. motors. 
Due consideration shall be given to the maximum brake 
torque which can be applied to the drive. 


17.4 Dynamic Response 


Where unusual drive arrangements are employed the 
dynamic response of the system should be analyzed 
to ensure that any additional loadings are identified 
and mitigated for operational requirements and life 
expectancy of crane. 


17.5 Drum Gear Alignment 


The effects of trolley frame and rope drum deflections 
on the alignment of the hoist drum gear and pinion shall 
be considered. 


15 3177 :2020 


18 MACHINING REQUIREMENTS OF GEARS 


18.1 Machining and Inspection 


All gears shall be preferably 20° pressure angle full 
depth tooth form and shall have a full root radius unless 
this compromises other design considerations. The wall 
thickness over the keyway of pinions shall be at least 
equal to the tooth depth and the rim thickness of gears 
shall be at least 1.2 times the tooth depth. Gears shall 
not have a shoulder or step left in the fillet area. 


18.2 All gears shall be hardened and machine cut 
and may be profile ground. The gears shall confirm 
to relevant Indian Standards. The gearing shall be 
designed for a service life compatible with the service 
life of the mechanism, the class of utilization and state 
of loading used for the mechanism, and having regard 
to the prime mover and brake. 


19 GEAR BOXES 


19.1 Material 


All gears shall be of cast or wrought steel or forged 
steel of low or medium carbon steel or alloy steel and 
suitably heat treated and/or case carburized. 


19.2 All gears shall be completely enclosed in gear 
boxes which shall be attached to rigid supports. All 
gear boxes except for drum ring gears shall be oil-tight 
and sealed with compound or gaskets. The bottom of 
the gear boxes shall be split horizontally above the oil 
level. Easily accessible drain plugs and breathers shall 
be provided. Oil level dipsticks shall go directly into 
the main body of gear box. 


19.3 Openings shall be provided in the top section 
for the inspection of gearing at mesh lines. Gear box 
inspection cover plates should provide reliable sealing 
and be easily opened and re-sealed. 


19.4 Splash oil lubrication of bearings may be used 
unless otherwise specified. Oil pumps shall be used, if 
vertical gearing exceeds two reductions. On horizontal 
gearing, the oil level shall be above the smallest gear. 
Oil seals shall be sized to allow replacement with split 
seals. Through bolts should be used to hold the gear 
cases together and to mount the gear box to its base. 
All gear cases shall be mounted on machined surfaces. 
Shims shall not be used. 


19.5 Gear box seats shall be of sufficient size to allow 
the installation of shear blocks to locate the gear box 
positively. Gear boxes shall be provided with lifting 
lugs that are suitable for use in lifting the whole gear 
case assembly without tilting. 


19.6 All pair of gearboxes shall be preferably helical, 
except for planetary portion of gearboxes shall be 
spur. The gears shall be automatically splash /forced 
oil lubricated. The gears shall be readily removable 


20 


and the boxes shall be oil tight. They shall be of rigid 
construction and fitted with inspection covers and 
lifting lugs, where necessary. The inspection covers 
shall be so positioned that the first and second pinion 
shafts can be inspected. Minimum and maximum oil 
level indicators and facilities for oil filling, oil drainage 
and air breathing shall be provided. All gear boxes 
shall be in totally enclosed construction. Teeth shall be 
machine cut, suitably hardened and tempered and shall 
conform to IS 4460 (Part 1 to 3) or AGMA. The surface 
hardness of pinion shall be minimum 270 BHN and 
that for gear shall be minimum 220 BHN. Difference 
of hardness of pinion and gear shall not be less than 20 
BHN (except for case carburized gears). The gear box 
mounting shall be machine cut, seated and positively 
located on machined surface. Material of the gear box 
housing shall be cast or fabricated. The fabricated gear 
boxes shall be stress relieved before machining. The 
internal surfaces of the gear box shall be painted with 
oil resisting paint. 


19.7 If desired by purchaser, molten metal handling 
crane, main hoist mechanism shall be provided with 
planetary gearbox with dual drive system to facilitate 
uninterrupted operation without overloading of the 
hoist mechanism, so that the main hoist can be operated 
with one motor at half the rated speed when other motor 
fails. 


19.8 Shaft mounted geared brake motor for travel drive 
in CT and LT may also be used. 


20 CRANE LUBRICATION SYSTEM 


20.1 Following types of lubrication system may be 
considered as per requirement: 
a) Point lubrication; 
b) Semi centralized ( Bunched ) lubrication; 
c) Dual line centralized motorized lubrication 
system; 
d) Dual line centralized lubrication system with 
manual pump; 
e) Rail track lubrication system; and 
f) Wire rope lubrication system. 


All lubrication lines shall be suitably located to prevent 
any mechanical damage. 


20.2 Provisions shall be made for lubricating all 
bearings unless sealed or lubricated for life, mating 
gears and chain and sprockets arrangements, where 
necessary easy access shall be provided. 


21 LINE SHAFTING AND COUPLINGS 


21.1 Floating Shaft 


Where possible, the flexible halves of half flexible 
couplings shall be mounted on the floating shaft. 


Couplings shall be located close to the bearings апа be 
provided with substantial removable guards which shall 
extend beyond the ends of the hubs and overlap with 
the coupling hub outer diameter. Where half-flexible 
couplings are used, the couplings shall be located close 
to the bearing on the end track and the adjacent line 
shaft bearing shall not be closed than 1 250 mm. 


21.2 The load shall be transmitted between couplings 
half by means of fitted bolts. For shaft speed below 400 
rpm, the following maximum bearing spacing shall be 
permitted: 


a) 3.5 m for 75 mm diameter; 

b) 4.25 m for 90 mm diameter; 

с) 4.5 m for 100 mm diameter; and 
d) 4.85 m for 115 mm diameter . 


21.3 For shaft speed in excess of 400 rpm, the above 
spacing shall be reduced as necessary to avoid harmonic 
vibrations. Supports for motor and gear reduction units 
shall be welded structural steel, rigidly connected to 
the crane girder. Bolts for fastening bearing brackets, 
motors and gear reduction unit shall be accessible from 
above the foot walk. Angular deflection of bridge line 
shafts at torque shall not exceed 0.3?/m of shaft length. 


21.4 For connection between the hoist gear box and 
rope drum the following options may be considered as 
required: 


a) Built in geared coupling; 
b) Barrel coupling; and 


c) Any other suitable flexible transmission system as 
per requirement of the purchaser or design. 


22 RAILS 


22.1 Rail shall be as per IS 3443 or equivalent, 
rectangular bar or square bar of weldable steel (of high 
tensile steel) may also be used depending on capacity 
and duty of crane. Rail joint shall be secured by 
clamping or welding. 


22.1.1 Joints on trolley rail shall be clamped /welded 
/ made by using standard joint bars. There shall be no 
bolt holes adjacent to the welded joint. 


22.2 For box girders, rails shall be fastened in place 
by suitable clamps or square / rectangular bars can be 
welded to top of girder. Suitable wear plate may be 
provided below rail so as to avoid wear and tear or 
girder top flange, if agreed between the manufacturer 
and the purchaser. 


22.21 The rail clamping may be of soft mounting 
system consist of pad and clips, if agreed between 
manufacturer and purchaser in lieu of standard steel rail 
clamps. The clamps shall be spaced at not more than 
900 mm between centres. 


21 


IS 3177 : 2020 


23 OPERATOR'S CABIN 


23.1 Type and Location 


Based on purchaser's requirement, the operator's 
cabin may be of the fixed / moving type, open / enclosed 


type. 


23.2 Structure 


The cabin shall be rigidly built of structural steel and 
fire proof material for molten metal crane and shall 
be braced to prevent movement between cabin and 
supporting members. It shall be supported by rivets or 
bolts іп shear. The head room of the cabin shall not be 
less than 2 m. 


23.2.1 Driver s Cabin 


23.2.2 Driver 5 Visibility 


Driver's cabin shall be designed so that the driver has a 
clear view of all working areas. 


23.2.3 Cabin Dispositions 


The driver's cabin shall have sufficient room for the 
driver to be able to reach or leave the controls without 
hindrance. Controls shall preferably be operated from 
a sitting position, but also from a standing, when 
necessary. 


23.2.3.1 Driver's cabin shall have a minimum head 
room of 2 m and shall be fitted with a guardrail of at 
least 1.0 m high. 


а) A protective shield shall be installed above the 
driver's cabin when there is any danger of falling 
object. 


b) The layout of the cabin and controls shall be 
ergonomically designed. 


23.2.4 Heat Insulated Material (For Molten Metal 
Handling Crane, if Required by Purchaser) 


The structural frame work of the driver's cabin shall 
be non-combustible material, and the side panels and 
roof may optionally be of fire resistance materials. The 
floor of the driver's cabin shall be covered with non- 
metallic, heat-insulating material. 


23.2.5 Glazed Windows and Entrances 


Entrances shall be protected against accidental opening 
sliding doors and out ward opening doors of driver's 
cabin must lead on the landing. The drivers cabin's 
windows shall be provided with suitable safety glass to 
avoid the risk of breakage. 


23.2.6 Anti-glare Lighting and Heating 


Driver's cabin shall be provided with adequate anti- 
glare lighting to allow handling of the controls and, if 
necessary, may be ventilated. 


15 3177 :2020 


23.2.7 Heat-proof 


Driver’s cabin which are exposed to radiant heat shall 
be protected heat radiation, and of a heat proof design, 
and if required by the purchaser air-conditioned may be 
provided to ensure tolerable working conditions. 


23.2.8 Following shall be provided at the appropriate 
location: 


a) Emergency stop and reset device; 


b) Electrically operated audio warning device, 
audible at minimum distance of 30 m; and 


c) Adequate illumination. 


23.3 In ladle cranes, other cranes handling hot materials 
and outdoor cranes, cabins shall be totally enclosed, 
unless otherwise specified. 


23.4 The cabin of outdoor cranes shall be weather proof. 
If the cabins are fitted with opening windows, these 
shall be hinged or made to slide as per manufacturer’s 
standard practise. If special vision panels are provided 
in the floor, they shall be suitably guarded. Arrangement 
shall be made to ensure that the whole exterior of the 
cabin glazing can be safely cleaned. Glasses shall be 
mounted with proper rubber seals/ beadings and shall 
be able to with stand vibration. All glazing shall be 
toughened plate glass of 6 mm minimum thickness 
conforming to IS 2553 (Part 1) and shall be installed 
from inside. Heat shield shall be provided below the 
cabin of hot metal handling crane. 


23.5 Cabin Access 


Access to open cabins via rung ladder or staircase from 
walkway, the entrance to the cabin shall be fitted with 
a door located for safe access. The cabin floor shall be 
extended outside the cabin on the side containing the 
door, and if necessary, sideways also to form a platform 
unless otherwise required. Suitable hand railing should 
be provided on the platform. 


23.6 Accessibility to the bridge platform shall be 
through the stairs. However, in case of space constraints 
ladders may be provided, if required. 


23.7 Visibility and Field of Vision 


Cabins shall be so designed that under all operating 
conditions the field of vision of the driver is adequate. 


23.8 Lighting, 
conditioning 


Heating, Ventilation and Air- 


Fixed service lighting shall be installed to provide glare 
free illumination in the crane cabin. АП cabins shall be 
provided with an air circulating fan of minimum sweep 
400 mm. АП air-conditioned cabins shall be fitted with 
a suitable hydraulic door closer and temp in the cabin 
shall be around 25°С. 


23.9 A suitable carbon dioxide (CO,) type fire 
extinguisher shall also be provided. 


22 


23.10 The cabin shall have a robust seat with a fixed 
or hinged or swivelling base and a durable upholstered 
squab. The seat shall be capable of withstanding severe 
braking force. 


24 GANGWAYS AND PLATFORMS 


24.1 Cabin Access 


24.1.1 Easy and safe access to the driver's cabin 
must possible in any position under normal working 
conditions. 


24.1.2 The driver's cabin shall be fitted with suitable 
emergency exit. 


24.1.3 Entry to the driver's cabin should be preferably 
from a platform at the same level as the floor of the 
cabin and provided with guard rails. 


24.2 Access to Gang Ways, Stair Ways and Platforms 


Gangways, stair ways and platforms must have safe 
access in any position. 


24.3 Maintenance Areas 


АП operating locations and all equipment of the crane 
which requires regular inspection or maintenance must 
be provided with safe access. Arrangement shall be 
provided to ensure that whole exterior of the cabin 
glass shall be safely cleaned without any additional 
scaffolding. 


24.3.1 Head Room 


Stair ways, gang ways and platforms shall have a head 
room of not less than 2 m and clear passage way of not 
less than 600 mm wide must be provided. 


24.3.2 Guard Rail 


Guard rails shall be not less than 1 m height and shall 
be provided with toe guards and intermediate rails. 


24.3.3 Slip-proof Surfaces 


Platform surfaces shall be suitably slip-proof. Holes, 
gaps and openings in the flooring shall be restricted in 
size so that a 20 mm diameter ball can't pass through. 


24.3.4 Power Line Protections 


When gang ways are located adjacent to power lines, 
these lines must be protected against accidental contact. 


25 GUARDING 


25.1 АП gear wheels, pinions and chain drives shall be 
totally enclosed. Effective guards shall be provided for 
revolving shafts and couplings. Long travel cross-shafts 
and couplings above the top platform shall be guarded 
wherever necessary. The sheaves of hook blocks shall 
be guarded to prevent the trapping of a hand between 
a sheave and the in-running rope and shall be enclosed 
except for rope opening. 


25.2 Safety features in hook blocks, pulleys and other 
load carrying devices. 


25.2.1 Prevent to Jumping 


Adequate means shall be provided to prevent the rope 
from jumping of the pulleys. 


25.2.2 Hand Guard 


An adequate guard shall be provided where there is any 
danger of a hand being trapped between the rope and 
the pulley of the hook block. 


25.2.3 Maintenance 


Rope pulleys shall be designed so as to be accessible 
for maintenance. 


25.2.4 Working Load Name Plate 


Inter changeable load carrying devices, such as, grabs, 
lifting magnets, tongs and lifting beams shall be 
permanently marked with their safe working load and 
dead weight and also, in case of grabs and buckets their 
capacity and name of manufactures. 


26 WEATHER PROTECTION 


For outdoor cranes, all electrical equipment shall be 
adequately protected from weather. All weather proof 
covers shall be easily removable. 


27 PAINTING 


27.1 Before dispatch of the crane, the complete crane 
covering structural, mechanical and electrical parts 
shall be thoroughly cleaned of all dirt, grease, scale 
and rust by shot blasting or chemical cleaning methods. 
Suitable number of coats of primer shall be given to 
all parts exposed to the weathering effects and if are 
not already treated earlier or effectively lubricated. At 
least two additional finishing coats of paint for indoor 
cranes/outdoor cranes of colour of customer’s choice 
shall be given on all primer painted surfaces. 


27.2 All moving parts up to the height of 5.0 m from 
working level or ground shall be painted in ‘Golden 
Yellow’ colour. The bright exposed parts of the crane 
shall be given one coat of rust inhibitor. Interior of all 
gear boxes shall be painted with one coat of oil resisting 
paint. Areas that are inaccessible after assembly or 
erection shall be treated before assembly or erection. 


27.3 Where the cranes are supplied for use in abnormal 
working conditions special protection may be necessary. 
Any additional requirements regarding painting shall be 
as agreed between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 
28 HANDLING FACILITIES 


28.1 Suitable structure at all four corners for handling 
the track wheels shall be provided for outdoor cranes. 


23 


IS 3177 : 2020 


However, for all outdoor goliath and semi-goliath 
cranes, this facility shall be provided. 


28.2 All cranes shall be provided with jack pad on both 
end carriages and trolley structures in such a way so 
as to facilitate removal of wheels, wheel bogie and 
compensating bogie. 


29 BRIDGE AND TROLLEY DRIVES 


29.1 Bridge and trolley drives arrangements may cover 
most types of crane drives regardless of the number of 
wheels. 


29.2 Bridge and Trolley Drive 


Bridge and trolley drive may consist of one of the 
following typical arrangements (see Fig. 8) and these 
arrangements cover most four or eight wheel crane 
drives: 


29.3 А1 Drive 


The motor is located near the centre of the bridge/ 
trolley and connected to a self-contained gear reduction 
unit located near the centre of the bridge/trolley. Output 
of the gear reduction shall be connected directly to 
the track wheel axle by means of suitable shafts and 
couplings. 


29.4 A2 Drive 


The motor is connected to a self contained gear 
reduction unit located near the centre of the bridge/ 
trolley. The track wheels shall be driven through gears 
pressed and keyed on their axles or by gears fastened 
to, or integral with, the track wheels and with pinions 
mounted on the end section of the cross-shaft. The 
end sections of the cross-shaft shall be connected by 
suitable couplings. 


29.5 A3 Drive 


The motor is located at the centre of the bridge/trolley 
and is connected to the cross-shaft and gear reduction 
units with suitable coupling. Self-contained gear 
reduction units located near each end of the bridge/ 
trolley shall be either directly connected to the wheel 
axle extension or connected to wheel axles by means of 
shafts in the suitable couplings. 


29.6 A4 Drive 


The motors are located near each end of the bridge/ 
trolley without torque shafts. The motors shall be 
connected to self-contained gear reduction units. 
The gear reduction unit shall be applied to the 
track wheels by means of both suitable shafts and 
couplings or directly mounted to the wheel axle 
shaft extension. Another variation of this drive 
would separate the high speed and final reductions 
by locating the motors near each end of the bridge 
without torque shafts. 


15 3177 :2020 


A 1 DRIVE 


€ CRANE 


Note - Other arrangement may also be considered if required. 


Fic. 8 TYPICAL ARRANGEMENT OF BRIDGE AND TROLLY DRIVE 


29.7 А5 Drive 


The motor is located near the centre of (һе bridge/ 
trolley and is connected to a self-contained gear 
reduction unit located near centre of the bridge/trolley. 
This reduction unit shall be connected by sections of 
cross-shaft having suitable couplings to self-contained 
gear reduction units located near each end of the crane, 
and these in turn connected to track wheel axle by 
means of shafts with suitable coupling. 


24 


29.8 46 Drive 


The motors аге located near each end of the bridge/ 
trolley and connected with a torque shaft. On the drive 
end, the motors shall be connected to self-contained 
gear reduction units by suitable couplings. The output 
of the gear reduction units shall be connected directly 
to the track wheel axle by means of suitable shafts and 
couplings. 


29.9 AT Drive 


The geared brake motors are mounted on the wheel 
shaft with torque arm to transmit the torque to the 
driving wheel. This arrangement is an alternative of A4 
drive (see 29.6) which is compact and ensure life time 
alignment of the drive. 


29.10 Percentage of driving wheels may be 16.66, 25, 
33.33, 50 or 100 depending on the requirement. While 
selecting the percentage of driving wheels, it shall be 
ensured that there is no skidding. 


30 TORSIONAL, 
VIBRATION 


DEFLECTION AND 


Natural frequency and amplitude of total torsional 
deflection of the drive system should be determined. 
Low frequencies and large total torsional deflections 
are undesirable for crane operation. 


31 MOTION LIMITING DEVICES 


Positively operated hoisting motion limiting devices 
shall be provided that stops the upward and downward 
motion when predetermined level is reached to prevent 
over winding or over unwinding. Pre-limit switch shall 
also be provided for slowing down before the final 
limits are actuated wherever control system permits 
variable speed. 
NOTE — The limiting device shall be regarded as a safety 
feature and not as a routine operational means of stopping. 
Where normal operation of the crane necessitates frequent 
approach to the upward limit, an additional motion limiting 
device shall be provided that operates independently and 
require manual settings. 


32 CROSS TRAVEL AND LONG TRAVEL 
LIMITING DEVICES 


The limiting devices shall prevent the following 
conditions: 


a) Over traversing and over travelling, or 


b) Collision where two or more crane/trolleys 
operating on the same track/ different track at 
different level in the same bay (if specified). 


Pre-limit switch shall also be provided for slowing 
down before the final limits are actuated wherever 
control system permits variable speed. 


33 LOAD LIMITING DEVICES 


Load limiting devices are recommended, if weights 
of objects to be lifted are not known accurately. When 
fitted, they shall sense the load on the crane by means 
other than the current consumed by the hoist motor. If 
the load lifted is more than SWL, load limiting devices 
shall stop further hoisting operation till the load is 
removed or reduced. If required by purchaser, load 
indication may be suitably provided. This arrangement 
is to be provided, if specifically asked by purchaser. 


25 


IS 3177 : 2020

following drawings and documents shall be submitted 
for approval of the purchase before manufacturing of 
the crane: 

a) GA drawings of the crane; 

b) GA drawings of crab/trolley;

SECTION 3 ELECTRICAL 
EQUIPMENT 


35 POWER SUPPLY 


35.1 General 


This standard deals with a.c. low voltage systems up 
to 1 000 V. The power supply system should comply 
with relevant Indian Standards. Voltage variation at the 
point of supply to crane DSL system be limited to 4 
5 percent of the rated voltage under normal operating 
conditions. The end user shall ensure this with respect 
to number of cranes in the bay with dedicated feeding 
transformer or feeder, etc. For applications with very 
long cabling distances it may be necessary to limit the 
voltage variation further. The allowed voltage drop 
(percent) in the different parts of the power supply need 
to be considered case by case. The type of the power 
supply grounding may have significant effects on the 
requirements of the crane electrification. The type 
should always be as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the supplier. For cranes with incoming power 
requirement higher than 1 000 kVA, for example, 
ladle crane, the system voltage should be designed 
preferably at 415/ 690 V a.c. in order to optimize the 
sizes of conductor, cables , motors and controls. 


35.2 DSL Systems and Accessories for Cranes 


35.2.1 General 


Down shop lead arrangement using Gl, copper, 
aluminum or steel sections with or without shrouding 
or by using flexible trailing cable arrangement or with 
drag chain/cable reeling drum may be used. 


15 3177 :2020 


35.2.2 Conductors 


Current conductor system or DSL system shall be 
provided either by the purchaser or by the crane 
manufacturer as agreed by them. Cranes operating on 
bare conductors shall be equipped with suitable guards 
to prevent ropes or suspended load coming in contact 
with the live conductors due to swing of the hook 
block. Down-shop conductors also shall be screened 
to prevent contact while handling long lengths of 
conducting materials from floor. 


35.2.3 Current Collectors 


Unless otherwise agreed to, all collector assembly shall 
be supplied by the crane manufacturer. The purchaser 
shall furnish relevant details depending upon the 
manufacturer’s scope of work. Collector rollers or shoes 
shall be so designed as to minimize/avoid sparking, 
shall be spring loaded/gravity type and shall be easily 
replaceable. Collector assembly shall be mounted on a 
rigid structure on the crane bridge. Necessary safe and 
convenient access shall be provided for maintenance 
or replacement of the collectors. Minimum two current 
collectors shall be provided per trolley line. Each 
collector shall be of 100 percent rating of crane total 
current load. 


35.2.4 Rating and size of DSL / Runway Conductor 


The total ampere load is determined with full load 
currents reduced by load diversity factor and duty cycle 
factor given in Table 10 and Table 11 respectively. The 
total ampere load shall be considered as per Table 12. 
After determination of the sequence of the motors with 
the largest output (ID), the amperages marked with 


an “Х”, plus basic loads for auxiliary load are added 
together i.e. I - EI, +21. 


Current rating of runway conductor = Total load current 
as per Table 12 X fi, x f, 


The selected current rating of the runway conductor 
may be derated by the temperature correction factor as 
per the manufacturer as applicable. 


NOTES 


1 In this clause, the rated current (1,) should be considered 
not necessarily to mean the name plate current of the motor 
but the current drawn by the motor at full rated load (that is, 
FLC corresponding to mechanical kW at rated ambient and 
duty). 

2 When squirrel cage motor is operated by variable voltage 
variable frequency converter, the full load current drawn from 
supply source by VFD line current should be considered for 
sizing of runway conductor

35.3.1 General 


Cross travel current collecting system shall be with 
bare conductors or with shrouded conductors or 
with trailing cable arrangement or with cable drag 
chain. The collection system shall be provided by the 
manufacturer. 


35.3.2 Conductors 


Cross travel conductors for the main trolley shall be 
mounted on the main bridge platform and not inside 
the main girders. Conductors for auxiliary crabs shall 
be mounted suitably above the level of auxiliary trolley 
rails. Cross travel conductors shall be arranged so that

35.3.3 Collector Assembly 


Collector assembly shall be rigidly mounted on 
the trolley and shall be provided with reasonable 
accessibility to all parts for maintenance purpose. 


35.4 Earthing 
35.4.1 General 


The crane structure, motor frames, and metal cases 
of all electrical equipment including metal conduit or 
cable guards shall be effectively connected to earth 
complying with Indian Electricity Rules,1956 (see IS 
3043). Preferably a ring earthing system to be provided 
on the crane. Each and every electrical equipment shall 
be connected to this earthing ring atleast at two points. A 
flexible metallic tube or duct may not form an effective 
earth connection. The crane wheels shall not be used 
as means of earthing. Where the crane is connected to 
the supply by flexible cord or flexible cable, the crane 
shall be connected to earth by means of a separate 
earthing conductor enclosed with the current carrying 
conductors. Travelling cranes connected to the supply 
through collectors (minimum two numbers) shall be

35.4.2 Control Circuit Earthing 


One end of the secondary winding of control circuit 
transformer shall be earthed. One end of the coil of all 
relays and contactors shall be connected to earth side of 
the control circuit supply and this connection shall not 
be interrupted by any fuse or contact. In the case of d.c. 
control circuits one pole of the rectifier shall be earthed. 


35.4.3 Magnet Earthing 


The magnet frame shall be bonded to the trolley by 
the earth connection via the magnet lead, the magnet 
coupling, the magnet cable and an extra slip-ring on the 
cable drum. 


35.5 Conductor Bars, Cable Reels and Flexible 
Cables 


The following five important considerations shall be 
taken into account in dimensioning insulated wires or 
cables: 

a) Temperature rise in normal condition; 


b) Temperature rise in faulty operation and on short- 
circuit; 


27 


15 3177 :2020 


с) Voltage drop; 
d) Cable grouping; and 
e) Motor full load current. 


35.5.1 The following clauses in IS 16504 (Part 32) 
define the basic requirements: 


a) Flexible cable (see 13.7); 


b) Collector wires, collector bars and slip ring 
assemblies (see 13.8); and 


c) Connections to cranes and between moving parts 
of the crane (see 14.4.3). 


According to IS 16504 (Part 32), wherever collector 
wires, conductor bars and slip-ring assemblies are 
installed as part of the protective bonding circuit, they 
shall not carry current in normal operation. Therefore, 
the protective conductor (PE) and the neutral conductor 
(N) shall each use a separate collector wire, collector bar 
or slip-ring. The continuity of the protective conductor 
circuit using sliding contacts shall be ensured by taking 
appropriate measures (for example, duplication of the 
current collector, continuity monitoring). The continuity 
of any protective bonding connection with sliding 
contacts shall be ensured for example, by duplication 
of the current collector (one set). Additionally, when 
sliding contacts are used to supply power to electronic 
drives, double collectors should be used to avoid noise 
and hardware failures which may occur, if a contact 
cuts off momentarily (2 sets of current collectors). 


35.6 Calculation of Cross-Section of Conductors 


35.6.1 These requirements apply both to the power 
supply to the crane and also to cabling within the crane. 
In general the selection of cable/conductors depend on 
the following: 

a) General operating conditions; 

b) Ambient air temperature; 

c) Methods of installation; 

d) Grouping; and 

e) Intermittent duty applications.

35.6.4 Calculation of the Cross-section in Relation to 
the Admissible Voltage Drop 


The voltage drop must be considered, paying attention 
to the fluctuation and the voltage drop within the 
power supply. For very long supply lines, not only 
the resistive but also the inductive part of the supply 
impedance need to be taken into account. Drop due to 
reactance should also be checked. The cross-section 
of the conductors should be determined by taking 


into account the mechanical strength required and 
the electrical load to be carried. Looping cable may 
be provided in parallel after checking the limit of 
voltage drop. When calculating the voltage drop, the 
most unfavourable position of the hoisting appliance in 
relation to the supply point must be considered. 


The voltage drop shall be limited to 3 percent on DSL 
and 2 percent on the crane (from current collector to 
motor terminals). The conductor size and/or number of 
feed points should be increased or even booster cables 
should be used in parallel to runway conductors in case 
the voltage drop is exceeding the limit value. 


Unless otherwise specified the maximum current 
density shall not exceed 0.42 A/mm? for rolled steel 
sections. The size of shrouded conductor, copper / 
aluminum headed conductor/GI conductor type DSL, 
the current rating as per manufacturer shall be followed.

minimum cross-section (C,,) of conductor can be 
calculated with the formula:

35.6.6 Calculation of the Minimum Cross-section in 
Relation to the Thermal Capacity of the Conductors 


When calculating the cross-section for the conductor 
bar, which supplies several hoisting appliances, the 
actual simultaneous operation of the drive motors must 
be taken into account. 


The maximum allowed conductor temperature shall not 
be exceeded during normal operation. Conductor cross- 
section should be selected according to manufacturers’ 
specifications.
